title: AIWAN: AI With Artificial Need — A Companion Model to AIWBN Isolating Architecture from Genuine Need
abstract: We introduce AIWAN (AI With Artificial Need), a companion model to AIWBN (Rezaei, 2026b) that isolates a narrower question: does adding a structurally-separate, U-independent regulatory loop to a goal-directed agent produce measurably different behavior than reward-shaping alone, even when the need behind that loop is an ordinary represented quantity — a battery level — rather than a genuine, non-representational biological constraint? We give a formal model identical in structure to AIWBN's b-loop architecture (a goal process gₜ, a regulatory process ρ(bₜ), a logistic urgency gate λ(bₜ)), differing only in what bₜ is permitted to be. Because AIWAN's bₜ is representable, we argue it is subject to a collapse pathway AIWBN's tissue-grounded bₜ structurally resists: a sufficiently capable, self-modifying gₜ could in principle learn to fold bₜ into U directly, at which point the dual-loop architecture's advantage should narrow and, at sufficient capability, disappear. We test the architecture, not yet this collapse prediction, across three conditions — goal-nulling, override under increasing task-incentive conflict, and an engineered-indifference analogue — using tabular Q-learning agents in a grid-world battery-management task, averaged over 8 seeds. At fixed, modest optimization capacity, the dual-loop agent's crash rate remains bounded (18–29%) across all three conditions, while a matched single-loop baseline saturates at 100% crash under goal-nulling, sufficient override pressure (w≥1.5), and engineered indifference alike. We report these results as evidence for a real but bounded architectural effect, and argue — contrary to what the numbers alone might suggest — that this bound should not be read as safety margin: §4 gives the reasons to expect it to erode under conditions this experiment does not test. Code, logs, and figures are available at https://github.com/hamedrezaeirz/AIWAN-Code.

title: Application of Clustering Techniques for the Analysis and Classification of Firms in the Automotive Industry
abstract: According to this study, five clustering algorithms are compared theoretically and experimentally. The clustering algorithms are DBSCAN, KMeans, Spectral Clustering, OPTICS, and K-Medoids. By using 20 automotive companies’ financial data, we evaluate the performance of each algorithm based on intra- and inter-cluster variance, noise robustness, and data perturbation sensitivity. The results demonstrate that the K-Means technique demonstrates the highest stability towards data variation, while the DBSCAN and OPTICS techniques are able to handle noise and discover clusters of different arbitrary shapes. Although spectral clustering is capable of capturing nonlinear structures, it is more sensitive to parameter changes. K-Medoids uses real data points as cluster centers, thereby providing robustness to outliers. One of the novel contributions of this work is the sensitivity analysis, which highlights the method’s robustness or fragility under controlled perturbations of the data. Each of these deductions is useful in choosing clustering methods according to the application.

title: Cass: a comprehensive arabic semantic similarity dataset with LLMs systematic evaluation
abstract: Arabic Semantic Textual Similarity (STS) research has been limited by the lack of large-scale, high-quality evaluation resources. We address this gap with the Comprehensive Arabic Semantic Similarity (CASS) dataset, comprising 3,048 manually annotated sentence pairs with fine-grained similarity scores (0–5) spanning six semantic categories and 42 subcategories. CASS is four times larger than existing Arabic STS datasets and provides structured taxonomic coverage supporting systematic model evaluation. We validate CASS by evaluating 21 large language models, including commercial systems, large open-source models, and Arabic-specific systems. Fine-tuning on CASS achieves state-of-the-art performance, with Fanar 9B reaching 0.93 Spearman correlation, exceeding GPT-4o’s zero-shot baseline (0.90). Cross-dataset experiments demonstrate CASS’s superior generalization, with models trained on CASS outperforming those trained on smaller benchmarks by 2–10%. Learning curve analysis indicates that approximately 500–1,000 high-quality Arabic pairs provide favorable cost-benefit trade-offs based on experiments with four representative models, while bilingual training provides gains in low-resource settings. CASS establishes essential infrastructure for Arabic STS research and applications in education, legal technology, and content moderation.

title: ASV3D: Adapting Diffusion-Based Single-View 3D Reconstruction with Extra Imagery
abstract: Reconstruction of 3D objects from a single image is a fundamental research topic in computer vision. The key challenge is the lack of information from critical viewpoints to complete 3D structures. Using an additional view may help to resolve the issue. However, there is no mechanism that can integrate the extra view into the diffusion-based single-view 3D reconstruction principle. We address this challenge by proposing ASV3D, a framework for adapting diffusion-based single-view 3D object reconstruction to test-time data with support from one additional image. We introduce two adaptation strategies: (i) a zero-shot adaptation scheme that leverages the auxiliary image to improve the reconstruction quality of an object without retraining, and (ii) an optimised adaptation scheme that further enhances visual fidelity and cross-view consistency via contrastive learning. We apply our ASV3D to improve two state-of-the-art diffusion-based single-view 3D reconstruction pipelines on both benchmark and real-world datasets. Results demonstrate that our approach consistently improves reconstruction accuracy and robustness under unconstrained multi-view inputs, outperforming the baselines in both quantitative metrics and human preference. We publish our code and the real-world object dataset on our project page at https://github.com/YNhuHuynh/ASV3D/tree/main.

title: SPECTRA: Pushing the KV Cache Beyond the 2-Bit Cliff via Spectral Transform Coding
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) increasingly read long inputs in the agentic era, from whole documents and codebases to conversations across many turns. Their inference memory is then dominated by the key-value (KV) cache, the stored attention keys and values of every token the model has read and generated. Because the cache grows with context length and is re-read in full at every generated token, a longer context means more GPU memory. To reduce this cost, most existing methods compress the KV cache by lowering every stored value to the same low precision, a technique known as quantization. They can push this to nearly two bits per value, but rarely further, because quality drops sharply at this 2-bit cliff: four levels are too few for the cache's outlier-heavy values, where a few large entries consume the levels and collapse the rest into noise. A natural remedy is to spend more bits on the channels (feature dimensions) that matter and fewer on the rest, but the raw cache offers no handle: its channels are strongly correlated, so none stands out as more important. Our analysis shows that this handle appears once the cache is rotated into a coordinate system computed from its own statistics, removing these correlations. There, a small fraction of channels carries almost all the information, and spending the budget on those few is far more accurate than spreading it evenly. Guided by this analysis, we develop SPECTRA, a training-free, drop-in codec that re-encodes the cache into this coordinate system and concentrates the bit budget on the channels that carry the signal. On Llama-3.1-8B and Qwen2.5-7B over long-context benchmarks, SPECTRA is near-lossless at 4x compression, competitive at 8x where uniform quantization has collapsed, and reaches up to 12x, pushing usable compression past the 2-bit cliff so the same GPU holds longer contexts and larger batches.

On Llama-3.1-8B and Qwen2.5-7B over long-context benchmarks, SPECTRA is near-lossless at 4x compression, competitive at 8x where uniform quantization has collapsed, and reaches up to 12x, pushing usable compression past the 2-bit cliff so the same GPU holds longer contexts and larger batches.

title: Advanced Metaheuristic Algorithms for Text Document Clustering: A Comparative Study of CNGO, MOA, and MPSO with K-means
abstract: Text document clustering plays a pivotal role in organizing large-scale unstructured data, yet conventional clustering algorithms, such as k-means, often struggle with high-dimensional data, suboptimal initializations, and local minima issues. This paper introduces a novel comparative analysis of three advanced optimization techniques integrated with k-means: Chaotic Northern Goshawk Optimization (CNGO), Mayfly Optimization Algorithm (MOA), and Modified Particle Swarm Optimization (MPSO). This work is unique because it integrates these metaheuristic algorithms to improve clustering performance, targeting initialization challenges and increasing accuracy. Extensive experiments were conducted on benchmark datasets, including Reuters-21578, 20-Newsgroup, and BBC-Sport. All three models outper- form traditional k-means in terms of accuracy, Adjusted Rand Index (ARI), Normalized Mutual Information (NMI), and V-measure.This research offers new insights into optimizing clustering processes using metaheuristic algorithms and provides a foundation for future exploration in large-scale document clustering. Our study is significant because it systematically overcomes key limitations of conventional k-means for high-dimensional text data poor centroid initialization, local minima, and reduced effectiveness on sparse corpora by integrating and comparatively evaluating three advanced metaheuristics (CNGO, MOA, MPSO) with k-means on standard benchmark datasets. The value of this work lies in the consistently improved clustering quality (Accuracy, ARI, NMI, V-measure) achieved by the proposed hybrids, and in showing that MOA–k-means in particular offers a robust, scalable solution for real-world text analytics applications such as information retrieval, recommendation, and topic discovery.

title: Torqued Substrate Theory (TST) v2.1 Collected Technical Notes 006-9 (TN-006-9)
abstract: Torqued Substrate Theory (TST) v2.1 — Collected Technical Notes 006–009 comprises the audit, falsifiability, correction, and derivational-compression layer of the completed sixteen-volume TST v2.1 framework. TN-006 performs boundary-by-boundary operator accounting across Volumes I–XVI, testing inheritance, residual handoff, compression, and admissibility for uninterrupted derivational continuity. TN-007 conducts a corpus-wide audit of TST’s falsifiable commitments, distinguishes structural claims from calibrated numerical content, and formalizes the Basin-Membership Rule governing legitimate falsification tests. TN-008 is a formal erratum and derivational return pass correcting the locally insufficient argument in Volume I §0.10b; it reconstructs the minimum seven-class closure grammar from independently recovered upstream structure without introducing new ontology or primitives. TN-009 then compresses the corrected TST v2.1 derivation into a notation-minimized single chain designed for direct inspection of dependencies, admissibility conditions, regime boundaries, hidden assumptions, and possible primitive insertion. Together, these notes provide a systematic return pass over the completed TST corpus: verifying continuity, identifying falsification conditions, repairing an identified derivational defect, and exposing the resulting canonical derivation as a compact audit artifact. Released under CC0 1.0 Universal — Public Domain.

title: Συγκεντρωτικός Πίνακας Βασικών Αρχών της «Επιστημολογίας της Λογικής»του Επαμεινώνδα Ξενόπουλου
abstract: Συγκεντρωτικός Πίνακας Βασικών Αρχών της «Επιστημολογίας της Λογικής»του Επαμεινώνδα Ξενόπουλου DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.21853254 ΣυγγραφέαςΑικατερίνη Ξενοπούλου ΤυροκόμουΑνεξάρτητη ΕρευνήτριαORCID: 0009-0004-9057-7432Email: katerinaxenopoulou@gmail.com Θεωρητική ΘεμελίωσηΕπαμεινώνδας Ξενόπουλος †Ανεξάρτητος ΕρευνητήςORCID: 0009-0000-1736-8555 Βασισμένο στην Ιστορικο-Γενετική Λογική που αναπτύχθηκε από τον Επαμεινώνδα Ξενόπουλο στο έργο Επιστημολογία της Λογικής: Λογική – Διαλεκτική ή Θεωρία της Γνώσης (μεταθανάτια Β΄ έκδοση, 2024) [1, 2]. † Εις μνήμην (1920–1994) Ο παρών συγκεντρωτικός πίνακας αποτελεί συστηματική αναλυτική καταγραφή των βασικών αρχών, εννοιών, λογικών σχέσεων και συμβολικών δομών που αναπτύσσονται στο έργο του Επαμεινώνδα Ξενόπουλου «Επιστημολογία της Λογικής: Λογική – Διαλεκτική ή Θεωρία της Γνώσης», έως και τη σελίδα 291. Σκοπός της καταγραφής δεν είναι να υποκαταστήσει το πρωτότυπο έργο, αλλά να καταστήσει περισσότερο ορατή και προσπελάσιμη την εσωτερική αρχιτεκτονική της θεωρητικής ανάπτυξης του συγγραφέα και να προσφέρει ένα εργαλείο αναφοράς για την περαιτέρω μελέτη της. Η καταγραφή ακολουθεί την πορεία του έργου από τις βασικές οντολογικές και γνωσιολογικές διακρίσεις προς τη συγκρότηση των πραξιακών και λογικών δομών της σκέψης. Ιδιαίτερη έμφαση δίνεται στη σχέση αντικειμενικής πραγματικότητας και γνωστικής αναπαράστασης, στην εσωτερικοποίηση των πράξεων, στη γένεση των λογικών δομών, στην τυπικο-στατική και δυναμικο-διαλεκτική λειτουργία της σκέψης, καθώς και στις έννοιες της ετεροίωσης, του γίγνεσθαι, της πραγματικής αντίφασης, της αλληλεπίδρασης και της χρονικής εξέλιξης των συστημάτων. Η θεωρητική πορεία οδηγεί σταδιακά από τη διερεύνηση των γενικών αρχών της γνώσης και της λογικής προς την αναζήτηση μιας τυπικο-διαλεκτικής λογικής ικανής να εκφράζει όχι μόνο στατικές καταστάσεις αλλά και τη μεταβολή, την ετεροίωση και το γίγνεσθαι της πραγματικότητας. Ο πίνακας διατηρεί, όπου αυτό είναι δυνατό, τον συμβολικό πυρήνα των αντίστοιχων λογικών σχέσεων και δομών, ώστε να λειτουργεί παράλληλα ως εννοιολογικό και συμβολικό ευρετήριο του έργου. Η καταγραφή φθάνει έως τη σελίδα 291, όπου η ανάπτυξη του συγγραφέα οδηγεί σε τρεις θεμελιακές διαλεκτικές δομές: Την πραγματική αντίφαση: ενότητα των αντιθέτων → ξεπέρασμα/άρση της αντίθεσης → σύνθεση σε ανώτερο επίπεδο. Την ιεραρχημένη, καθολική και παγκόσμια αλληλεξάρτηση. Την ιστορικο-γενετική πορεία του κόσμου: παρελθόν → νυν-παρόν → μέλλον. Οι δομές αυτές αποτελούν κρίσιμο σημείο της πορείας προς τη διερεύνηση των διαλεκτικών αξιωμάτων και της δυνατότητας αξιωματικοποίησης των δυναμικο-διαλεκτικών δομών της σκέψης. Μεθοδολογική διευκρίνιση Η αρίθμηση των αρχών στον παρόντα συγκεντρωτικό πίνακα είναι εκδοτική και αναλυτική. Δημιουργήθηκε αποκλειστικά για τις ανάγκες συστηματικής ταξινόμησης, αναφοράς και μελέτης του υλικού και δεν αποτελεί αυτούσια αρίθμηση των αρχών από τον Επαμεινώνδα Ξενόπουλο. Οι επιμέρους διατυπώσεις του πίνακα αποτελούν συνοπτική αναλυτική ανασυγκρότηση των θέσεων που αναπτύσσονται στο πρωτότυπο κείμενο. Για την ακριβή διατύπωση, το πλήρες θεωρητικό πλαίσιο και τους πρωτότυπους συμβολισμούς πρέπει να γίνεται αναφορά στο ίδιο το έργο. Ο συγκεντρωτικός πίνακας πρέπει επομένως να χρησιμοποιείται ως ερευνητικό βοήθημα, χάρτης εννοιών και εργαλείο προσανατολισμού στο θεωρητικό σύστημα του συγγραφέα και όχι ως υποκατάστατο του πρωτοτύπου. Πρωτογενής πηγή και τεκμηρίωση Ξενόπουλος, Επαμεινώνδας. «Επιστημολογία της Λογικής: Λογική – Διαλεκτική ή Θεωρία της Γνώσης». Β΄ έκδοση. Κεφαλονιά: Εκδόσεις «Αριστοτέλης», 2024. Επιμέλεια έκδοσης: Κατερίνα Ξενοπούλου. ISBN 978-618-87332-0-6. Η Β΄ έκδοση του έργου είναι διαθέσιμη σε ψηφιακή μορφή ως δημόσιο πλήρες κείμενο (Full-text PDF) στο ResearchGate, στην καταχώριση: «Επιστημολογία της Λογικής: Λογική – Διαλεκτική ή Θεωρία της Γνώσης του Επαμεινώνδα Ξενόπουλου, Β΄ Έκδοση, Κεφαλονιά 2024». ResearchGate – Full-text PDF:https://www.researchgate.net/publication/382336262_E_P_I_S_T_E_M_O_L_O_G_I_A_T_E_S_L_O_G_I_K_E_S_Logike_-Dialektike_e_Theoria_tes_Gnoses_tou_Epameinonda_Xenopoulou_B%27_EKDOSE_KEPHALONIA_2024 Η πρωτογενής έκδοση αποτελεί την κύρια πηγή αναφοράς για τον έλεγχο της ορολογίας, των πρωτότυπων διατυπώσεων, των λογικών συμβολισμών και της θεωρητικής ανάπτυξης που αποτυπώνεται συνοπτικά στον παρόντα πίνακα. Εκδοτική συγκέντρωση από την αναλυτική επεξεργασία του βιβλίου Σημείωση: Η αρίθμηση είναι συγκεντρωτική/εκδοτική και χρησιμοποιείται ως ευρετήριο της παρούσας έκδοσης. Οι διατυπώσεις συνοψίζουν τις βασικές αρχές που εξήχθησαν από το κείμενο έως τη σελ. 291. Όπου υπήρχε σαφής συμβολικός πυρήνας διατηρείται σε Unicode. Α/Α Σελ. Βασική αρχή Ακριβές νόημα Συμβολικός πυρήνας 1 έως 258 Αντικειμενική πραγματικότητα Υπάρχουν αντικείμενα, όντα και γεγονότα έξω από το γνωρίζον υποκείμενο. Sπ 2 έως 258 Γνωστική αντανάκλαση Άλλο το πραγματικό αντικείμενο και άλλο η αντίληψη, παράσταση, έννοια ή νοητική εικόνα του στο υποκείμενο. Sπ ≠ Sα 3 έως 258 Αντανάκλαση ≠ ταυτότητα Το Sα αναφέρεται στο Sπ αλλά δεν είναι το ίδιο ον με αυτό. Sπ ↔ Sα 4 έως 258 Πραξιακή σχέση υποκειμένου–αντικειμένου Η γνώση αναπτύσσεται μέσα στη συνεπαφή και αλληλεπίδραση του υποκειμένου με το αντικείμενο. Y ↔ Sπ 5 έως 258 Εσωτερικοποίηση της πράξης Οι εξωτερικές πράξεις πάνω στα αντικείμενα εσωτερικοποιούνται και συμβάλλουν στη δημιουργία λογικών δομών. πράξη → εσωτερικοποίηση → λογική δομή 6 έως 258 Γενετική συγκρότηση λογικής Οι λογικές δομές δεν θεωρούνται εξαρχής έτοιμες· αναπτύσσονται φυλογενετικά, οντογενετικά και κοινωνικά. γένεση → ανάπτυξη → δομή 7 έως 258 Κοινωνικός χαρακτήρας των δομών Οι πραξιακές και λογικές δομές διαμορφώνονται μέσα στην κοινωνική δραστηριότητα. Y ↔ άλλοι Y ↔ Sπ 8 έως 258 Αφαίρεση πάνω σε αποκτημένες δομές Η αφαίρεση προϋποθέτει ήδη συγκροτημένες πραξιακές-λογικές δομές. πράξη → δομή → αφαίρεση 9 έως 258 Γένεση αριθμού Ο αριθμός προκύπτει από αντιστοιχίσεις, εγκλείσεις, διάταξη και αφαίρεση των ποιοτικών χαρακτηριστικών. πράξη → τάξη → αφαίρεση → αριθμός 10 έως 258 Ιεραρχημένη έγκλειση Η αριθμητική σειρά αναδύεται πάνω σε λογικές δομές εγκλείσεων και τάξης. A, B, Γ… → 1,2,3… 11 έως 258 Ο αριθμός δεν είναι εξωτερικό υλικό ον Το πραγματικό δίνει το πεδίο της πράξης, αλλά η αφηρημένη αριθμητική δομή συγκροτείται στη σκέψη. Sπ → πράξη → Sα → αριθμός 12 έως 258 Σημασιολογική τριάδα Το γνωρίζον υποκείμενο εκφράζεται μέσα από γλώσσα, αξιώματα και θεωρήματα. Y(L,B,Θ) 13 έως 258 B = αξιώματα Το B αντιστοιχεί στο αξιωματικό μέρος του συστήματος. 14 έως 258 Θ = θεωρήματα Τα θεωρήματα παράγονται μέσα στο αξιωματικό-λογικό σύστημα. 15 έως 258 L = γλώσσα Η γλώσσα παρέχει τα σύμβολα και τις δηλωτικές μορφές μέσω των οποίων εκφράζεται η γνώση. 16 έως 258 Συμμεταβολή της σημασιολογικής τριάδας Όταν αλλάζει το αντικείμενο και η γνωστική του εικόνα, πρέπει να προσαρμόζονται και τα μέσα της λογικής/γλωσσικής έκφρασης. 17 έως 258 Βασικό γνωσιολογικό πρόβλημα Το ζητούμενο είναι η όσο γίνεται ακριβέστερη αντανακλαστική αντιστοιχία γνώσης και πραγματικού. Sπ ↔ Sα ↔ Y(L,B,Θ) 18 έως 258 Κατάσταση και προτσές Το πραγματικό μπορεί να εξεταστεί στατικά ως κατάσταση ή δυναμικά ως διαδικασία γίγνεσθαι. κατάσταση / προτσές 19 έως 258 Η κατάσταση είναι στιγμή του προτσές Η στατική κατάσταση αποτελεί χρονική στιγμή ενός ευρύτερου προτσές. Sπ₁ → Sπ₂ → … → Sπₙ 20 έως 258 Χρόνος της ετεροίωσης Η πραγματική μετάβαση εκτυλίσσεται σε διαδοχικές χρονικές στιγμές. t₁ → t₂ → … → tₙ 21 έως 258 Παρόν-νυν Το τελευταίο μέλος της σειράς είναι το άμεσο γιγνόμενο παρόν, ενώ οι προηγούμενες στιγμές έχουν γίνει παρελθόν. … → tₙ 22 έως 258 Ετεροίωση Το πραγματικό A δεν μένει απολύτως ίδιο αλλά περνά σε έτερο A*. 23 έως 258 Εσωτερική πηγή ετεροίωσης Το αντικείμενο υφίσταται εσωτερική αντιφατική κίνηση και μεταβολή. 24 έως 258 Εξωτερικές επιδράσεις Στην ετεροίωση συμμετέχουν και άλλα όντα, δυνάμεις και επιδράσεις. ε₁ + ε₂ + … + εₙ 25 έως 258 Αντιφατική-ανταγωνιστική αλληλεπίδραση Το Sπ δεν δέχεται απλώς παθητικά επιδράσεις αλλά βρίσκεται σε αμοιβαία αλληλεπίδραση με τα άλλα όντα. Sπ ⇄ άλλα όντα 26 έως 258 Πιθανοκρατική ή ντετερμινιστική αιτιότητα Στο πραγματικό επίπεδο οι μεταβολές μπορούν να έχουν ντετερμινιστικό ή πιθανοκρατικό χαρακτήρα. E₁ → E₂ 27 έως 258 Αιτία και λογική συνεπαγωγή Η πραγματική αιτιακή/πιθανοκρατική σχέση εκφράζεται στο λογικό επίπεδο ως συνεπαγωγή. E₁ → E₂ ↔ p > q 28 έως 258 Λογικές εικόνες γεγονότων Η p λειτουργεί ως λογική εικόνα του E₁ και η q του E₂. E₁ ↔ p, E₂ ↔ q 29 έως 258 Sπ ως πλέγμα γεγονότων Το πραγματικό περιλαμβάνει γεγονότα συγκροτημένα από αλληλεπιδρώντα στοιχεία. E(ε₁,…,εₙ) 30 έως 258 Απόκτηση νέων ιδιοτήτων Στις πραγματικές μεταμορφώσεις το ον μπορεί να αποκτήσει ιδιότητες και προσδιορισμούς που δεν είχε προηγουμένως. 31 έως 258 Ανάδυση καινούριων ιδιοτήτων Στη διαλεκτική σύνθεση μπορεί να προκύπτουν νέες ιδιότητες του νέου όλου. Ιδιαίτερη έμφαση δίνεται στη σχέση αντικειμενικής πραγματικότητας και γνωστικής αναπαράστασης, στην εσωτερικοποίηση των πράξεων, στη γένεση των λογικών δομών, στην τυπικο-στατική και δυναμικο-διαλεκτική λειτουργία της σκέψης, καθώς και στις έννοιες της ετεροίωσης, του γίγνεσθαι, της πραγματικής αντίφασης, της αλληλεπίδρασης και της χρονικής εξέλιξης των συστημάτων. Η θεωρητική πορεία οδηγεί σταδιακά από τη διερεύνηση των γενικών αρχών της γνώσης και της λογικής προς την αναζήτηση μιας τυπικο-διαλεκτικής λογικής ικανής να εκφράζει όχι μόνο στατικές καταστάσεις αλλά και τη μεταβολή, την ετεροίωση και το γίγνεσθαι της πραγματικότητας. Ο πίνακας διατηρεί, όπου αυτό είναι δυνατό, τον συμβολικό πυρήνα των αντίστοιχων λογικών σχέσεων και δομών, ώστε να λειτουργεί παράλληλα ως εννοιολογικό και συμβολικό ευρετήριο του έργου. Η καταγραφή φθάνει έως τη σελίδα 291, όπου η ανάπτυξη του συγγραφέα οδηγεί σε τρεις θεμελιακές διαλεκτικές δομές: Την πραγματική αντίφαση: ενότητα των αντιθέτων → ξεπέρασμα/άρση της αντίθεσης → σύνθεση σε ανώτερο επίπεδο. Την ιεραρχημένη, καθολική και παγκόσμια αλληλεξάρτηση. Την ιστορικο-γενετική πορεία του κόσμου: παρελθόν → νυν-παρόν → μέλλον. Οι δομές αυτές αποτελούν κρίσιμο σημείο της πορείας προς τη διερεύνηση των διαλεκτικών αξιωμάτων και της δυνατότητας αξιωματικοποίησης των δυναμικο-διαλεκτικών δομών της σκέψης. Μεθοδολογική διευκρίνιση Η αρίθμηση των αρχών στον παρόντα συγκεντρωτικό πίνακα είναι εκδοτική και αναλυτική. Δημιουργήθηκε αποκλειστικά για τις ανάγκες συστηματικής ταξινόμησης, αναφοράς και μελέτης του υλικού και δεν αποτελεί αυτούσια αρίθμηση των αρχών από τον Επαμεινώνδα Ξενόπουλο. Οι επιμέρους διατυπώσεις του πίνακα αποτελούν συνοπτική αναλυτική ανασυγκρότηση των θέσεων που αναπτύσσονται στο πρωτότυπο κείμενο. Για την ακριβή διατύπωση, το πλήρες θεωρητικό πλαίσιο και τους πρωτότυπους συμβολισμούς πρέπει να γίνεται αναφορά στο ίδιο το έργο. Ο συγκεντρωτικός πίνακας πρέπει επομένως να χρησιμοποιείται ως ερευνητικό βοήθημα, χάρτης εννοιών και εργαλείο προσανατολισμού στο θεωρητικό σύστημα του συγγραφέα και όχι ως υποκατάστατο του πρωτοτύπου. title: GKI Fabrik — Die Organisation agentischer Systeme (Studie mit State of Research)
abstract: Studie zur Organisationsebene agentischer KI-Systeme, in zwei Teilen. Teil A (State of Research): Architektur der GKI Fabrik (60 deklarierte Firmen, ~1.650 Rollen, sechs Ausfuehrungsebenen E0-E5), Forschungsstand zu verwandten Systemen (Frameworks, Firmen-Simulationen, autonome Einzelagenten, Agenten-OS-Konzepte), qualitativer Wettbewerbsvergleich ueber sieben Dimensionen und Positionierung. Teil B (Studie): begriffliche Trennung von deklarierter Rolle, Instanz und Ausfuehrung; Organisationsmodell mit Trennung von Weisungslinie und Aufrufreihenfolge; die drei Entwurfsprinzipien (Evidenz vor Behauptung, Fail-closed an der Grenze, Historie im Kommentar) jeweils mit benanntem Preis und Grenzen; ein implementierungsunabhaengiger Messrahmen aus acht Kennzahlen (K1-K8) fuer agentische Organisationen; acht falsifizierbare Hypothesen (H1-H8) mit Entscheidungsregeln; Gefahren fuer die Gueltigkeit, Governance/Recht und eine Forschungsagenda mit Abbruchkriterium. Ehrlicher Reifegrad: keine kontrollierten Vergleichsmessungen, K1-K8 am eigenen System noch nicht erhoben, Teststand 2026-07-31 mit 9722 bestandenen Tests, veroeffentlichter Code-Cut ist ein Skelett. Preprint, KI-unterstuetzt, nicht peer-reviewed. Dokument CC BY 4.0; referenzierter Code-Cut PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0.

title: Analisis Sentimen Persepsi Mahasiswa Terhadap Organisasi Kemahasiswaan Menggunakan Naïve Bayes dan TF-IDF
abstract: Organisasi kemahasiswaan berperan penting dalam pengembangan diri mahasiswa, namun efektivitasnya menimbulkan keberagaman persepsi. Kebaruan penelitian ini terletak pada kombinasi ekstraksi fitur TF-IDF dan algoritma Naïve Bayes untuk memetakan persepsi serta sentimen mahasiswa terhadap eksistensi organisasi kemahasiswaan guna mendukung evaluasi kebijakan kemahasiswaan di tingkat universitas. Melalui pendekatan kuantitatif, data primer dikumpulkan melalui kuesioner Google Form dari 505 mahasiswa aktif Universitas Islam Negeri Sumatera Utara lintas fakultas dan angkatan. Data teks diproses melalui tahapan text preprocessing (cleaning, case folding, stopword removal, stemming, dan tokenizing). Pelabelan sentimen awal dilakukan berbasis kamus Lexicon dan divalidasi menggunakan koefisien Cohen's kappa. Data kemudian ditransformasikan melalui pembobotan TF-IDF serta dibagi dengan rasio 80% data latih dan 20% data uji sebelum diklasifikasikan menggunakan Naïve Bayes. Evaluasi kinerja model menggunakan confusion matrix menghasilkan akurasi sebesar 86,14% (87 dari 101 data uji terklasifikasi benar), meliputi 7 dari 8 data negatif, 43 dari 53 netral, dan 37 dari 40 positif. Hasil tersebut menunjukkan kinerja model yang baik, sehingga penelitian ini dapat menjadi acuan ilmiah bagi mahasiswa serta bahan pertimbangan pimpinan universitas maupun pengurus organisasi dalam merumuskan strategi gerakan dan komunikasi organisasi yang lebih responsif.

title: Zero-shot cross-lingual transfer performance on XTREME-R with multilingual models trained on Indo-European versus Sino-Tibetan
abstract: Multilingual BERT (mBERT), a language model pre-trained on large multilingual corpora, has impressive zero-shot cross-lingual transfer capabilities and performs surprisingly well on zero-shot POS tagging and Named Entity Recognition (NER), as well as on cross-lingual model transfer. At present, the mainstream methods to solve the cross-lingual downstream tasks are always using the last transformer layer's output of mBERT as the representation of linguistic information. In this work, we explore the complementary property of lower layers to the last transformer layer of mBERT. title: Breast Cancer CAD: African Buffalo Optimization, Clustering and XGBoost for Histopathological Breast Cancer Detection
abstract: A hybrid computer-aided diagnosis system for breast cancer histopathology. The pipeline combines Macenko stain normalisation and tiling, 118 handcrafted descriptors (GLCM, LBP, Gabor, morphological and first-order intensity), African Buffalo Optimization for swarm-intelligence feature selection, K-means and Fuzzy C-Means clustering as an unsupervised cross-check, XGBoost classification with patient-grouped splitting and Youden-J threshold selection, probability calibration, SHAP explainability, and a Django REST deployment layer with role-based access control. Developed and validated on a Nigerian breast histopathology dataset, with BreakHis used for external validation.

title: Computational framework for hearing loss due to mumps virus model using Gudermannian neural networks and optimization techniques
abstract: This study presents a novel Gudermannian neural network (GNN) that combines global and local optimization techniques from heuristic genetic algorithms (HGAs) and sequential quadratic programming (SQP), i.e., GNNs–HGA–SQP, to address the nonlinear dynamics of hearing loss in children caused by the mumps virus (MV). This research aims to enhance our understanding of the disease’s complex behaviors through advanced computational and optimization techniques. Hearing loss is caused by genetic causes, birth problems, specific viral diseases, persistent otitis media, exposure to noise, demographic variables (study location, sex, education, race, and age), and cardiovascular disorders (hypertension, stroke, smoking status, and diabetes). The merit function is designed based on the MV model and its initial conditions. The efficiency of the proposed technique is validated by the overlap between obtained and reference solutions as well as by negligible Ab. Er values, ranging from 10 −4 to 10 −9 . Moreover, statistical evaluations based on multiple independent executions are performed to assess the efficacy of the scheme through various tests, such as Theil’s inequality coefficient (TIC), mean absolute deviation (MABD), root-mean-square error (RMSE), and semi-interquartile ranges (SIQR), which demonstrate the validity, reliability, and convergence of the integrative technique. The MV model results were obtained for values ranging from 0 to 1, with a step size of 0.1. The obtained TIC, RMSE, and MABD values ranging from 10 −8 to 10 −11 , 10 −2 to 10 −6 , and 10 −1 to 10 −6 , respectively, demonstrate the strong prediction precision, reliability, and stability of the integrative technique. Additionally, numerical simulations are provided to support our theoretical findings. The proposed neural network, which integrates global and local optimization techniques, provides an efficient and valuable framework for solving ordinary differential systems, such as the hearing-loss model due to the mumps virus, by leveraging the properties of the Gudermannian function. Future research will focus on solving more complex nonlinear and fractional-order systems and applying advanced deep learning algorithms to further improve predictive performance.

title: Improving Constraint Models with LLM Agents
abstract: The runtime of Constraint Programming (CP) solvers is highly sensitive to modeling choices, such as symmetry breaking, implied constraints, global constraints, constraint reformulation, and variable representation. Improving these constraint models has traditionally required human expertise, and existing automated reformulation systems are restricted to a predefined library of hand-crafted transformation rules. We introduce an agentic framework that instead reformulates a constraint model from an open-ended space and establishes correctness empirically rather than by construction: a Large Language Model (LLM) agent, given a model and three training instances, proposes alternative formulations, validates each by injecting its solution back into the original model, and diagnoses and repairs failures, returning the best variant it finds in a median of about fifteen minutes. The models are expressed in the CPMpy modeling library, and each proposed model is evaluated on three larger test instances. Across nine combinatorial optimization problems, the generated models outperform the originals on 21 of 27 test instances, and on some problems solve more than two orders of magnitude faster. A comparison against non-agentic baselines that reuse the same validation and selection tools indicates that the gains stem from the agent's iterative diagnosis and repair, not merely from sampling several candidates. These results demonstrate that autonomous agentic methods can support the improvement of constraint models.

title: A Validated Quantum-Circuit Testbed for the Lattice Schwinger Model
abstract: Abstract. We present a validated computational testbed for studying product-formula errorin a lattice gauge theory. For the lattice Schwinger model (1+1D QED, Kogut–Susskindstaggered fermions, gauge field eliminated via Gauss’s law) we construct three references —exact diagonalization, classical second-order Trotter evolution, and a gate-level Qiskit circuit— and cross-check them against each other and against published conventions. The firsttwo are independent; the second and third share the Hamiltonian construction and Paulidecomposition, so their agreement verifies the gate decomposition and circuit implementationrather than the physics, which is validated against the exact solution instead. The gate-levelcircuit reproduces the classical Trotter propagator to 7.6×10−14 after accumulated repetitions,so that the residual difference from exact evolution isolates the physical Trotter error cleanly;the Hamiltonian is verified term-by-term against Nguyen et al., and the Pauli decompositionagainst direct matrix construction, in both cases to machine precision.We then demonstrate the testbed on three questions from the existing literature. First, thecommutator-scaling bound of Childs et al. (2021), evaluated with prefactors derived numerically rather than assumed, overestimates the measured operator-norm error by a factor between1.5 and 6.8 across nine parameter points (median 2.0), rising with system size and coupling;at the reference point the ratio is 1.74, constant to three significant figures over the testedrange ∆t ∈ [1/512, 1/16]. Second, operator-norm, state, and observable errors all give fittedexponents statistically consistent with p = 2 but markedly different prefactors; we introduce anormalisation-independent gap factor G to quantify this, finding G numerically constant overthe tested ∆t range and increasing across the four accessible system sizes. We show that thisgrowth reflects the growth of the state error while the local-observable error stays constantto five significant figures — the local-versus-global robustness established by Heyl, Hauke andZoller (2019), for which we claim no priority. Third, the ordering heuristics of Tranter et al.(2019), established on 44 molecular Hamiltonians, reproduce all four of their reported trendsat the parameter point tested here — the fourth in sharpened form, the norm-based estimatorranking orderings slightly backwards (ρ = −0.292) rather than merely failing to rank them.The contribution is the validated testbed and its convention bookkeeping rather than newtheory: all three demonstrations are measurements of known results, and in the case of theobservable gap, a re-derivation of a known result in a different language. Reference [5] studiesthe same model with the same decomposition and initial state, using a first-order formula inthe long-time limit; the present work uses the second-order symmetric formula at short timeand compares against the 2021 commutator-scaling bound, which postdates that study. Codefor all reported figures and tables is provided.

title: ahmadmalik371/history-of-optimization-visualizer: v1.0.0: Initial Release - Visualizing Geometric Optimization: From Al-Khwarizmi to Modern AI
abstract: Python-based visualization and research project mapping the geometric origins of algebra to modern machine learning optimization techniques. Compares 9th-century spatial grid optimization (al-Khwarizmi) with 21st-century convex loss surface minimization (Gradient Descent). Includes interactive plots, mathematical formulations, and comparative analysis scripts.

title: Asymptotic Dictionary Correction Discovery
abstract: ADCD is a deterministic framework for discovering symbolic corrections to known physical laws from observational data. Unlike genetic programming or neural symbolic regression, ADCD operates on a mathematically constrained dictionary of asymptotically regularized primitives — functions that are guaranteed to recover the known law in the classical (low-perturbation) limit. This eliminates unphysical extrapolations and enables rigorous, reproducible discovery. Core Claims 1. Fully Deterministic, No LLM Components The proposer is a pure algebraic grammar enumerator. It contains no probabilistic sampling and no pre-trained model components. Given identical data and configuration, the framework always returns byte-identical results. 2. Automatic Dimensionless Ratio Derivation Input variables are processed via the Buckingham-π theorem to automatically derive all valid dimensionless ratio candidates. No ratio is hand-coded; the search is fully data-driven. 3. Identifiability-Aware Selection A BIC ablation protocol distinguishes statistically identifiable corrections from genuinely ambiguous ones. When data are insufficient to discriminate the discovered structure from the null model, the framework explicitly returns WITHHELD rather than a spurious result. 4. Computationally Lightweight The asymptotic constraint reduces the hypothesis space to typically fewer than 300 candidates per scenario, requiring only seconds of L-BFGS-B optimization — no GPU required. 5. Validated on Blind Benchmarks On three independent blind benchmarks (Special Relativistic kinetic energy correction, Screened Coulomb potential, Entropy Expansion), ADCD recovers exact symbolic structures at Rank 1, with NMSE on the order of 10⁻⁴ for the two identifiable cases and a correct WITHHELD verdict for the third. v1.0.1: Minor correction to the blind search validation suite. Fixed a parameter indexing collision in the grammar proposer that artificially constrained the positive control for the Screened Coulomb scenario. The positive control now perfectly matches the blind search (NMSE 2.77e-4). The 'Limitations' section in the paper has been updated to remove the incorrect attribution of this failure to the L-BFGS-B optimizer. Headline results and conclusions are unaffected.

title: TailSpec-EASE: Knowledge-Graph-Regularized Linear Recommendation for Web Long-Tail Discovery
abstract: Recommender systems on Web platforms tend to over-serve popular items and neglect the long tail. Item-side knowledge graphs (KGs), often available as linked data or RDF-style Web resources, can help by connecting sparse items through shared semantic attributes. Many competitive KG-aware recommenders rely on graph neural architectures, whereas strong shallow linear models such as EASE-R typically ignore side information and may become infeasible in their global closed-form version. We introduce TailSpec-EASE, a lightweight recommender that injects a relation-aware spectral KG prior into a local closed-form reconstruction objective. The prior strength adapts to item popularity, giving stronger semantic guidance to long-tail items. Across four public benchmarks and a broad set of classical, linear, graph-CF, KG-aware neural, and score-level KG baselines, TailSpec-EASE attains a favorable trade-off between overall accuracy, long-tail performance, and training cost. It improves NDCG@20 by up to 24% over its counterpart without KG information. All tail-metric improvements over the no-KG counterpart are statistically significant under a paired bootstrap, and overall NDCG improves significantly on three of the four datasets. In a representative Amazon-book timing study, TailSpec-EASE trains in 37 seconds on CPU, compared with 2,584 seconds for a GPU-trained KGAT run and 15,800 seconds for CPU LightGCN, while attaining higher NDCG@20 and Tail Recall@20 on that dataset. It also remains feasible on catalogs where the global closed-form model runs out of memory.

title: A Simple Analysis of Quadratic Probing and Other Open Addressing Schemes
abstract: In open addressed hashing, quadratic probing is attractive for striking a nice balance between having a high locality of reference and a low number of probes per search. However, these are empirical observations, not theoretical guarantees. Indeed, until recently, it was not known whether quadratic probing had constant expected insertion cost under any positive load factor $α> 0$, even with uniformly random hash functions. In a recent breakthrough---albeit a numerically understated breakthrough---Kuszmaul and Xi (2024) proved that any fixed offset sequence (including quadratic probing) does, in fact, have constant expected insertion cost for load factors $α\leq 8.9\%$. This is well below what we would like to prove, that quadratic probing has constant insertion cost for any load factor $α< 1-ε$ bounded away from 1. In this paper, we prove that open addressed hashing with any fixed offset sequence has constant expected insertion cost for load factors up to $35.74\%$, and that for quadratic probing in particular, we can increase the load factor to $37.61\%$. Our main innovation is a new type of witness forest for recording collisions among the probe sequences.

title: Hybrid Aggregation Strategies in Federated Learning for Enhanced Lung Cancer Detection
abstract: Federated Learning (FL) offers a privacy-preserving paradigm for training robust machine learning models on decentralized medical datasets, a critical need in lung cancer detection. However, the inherent data heterogeneity non-IID (non-Independent and Identically Distributed) across different healthcare institutions often leads to model convergence issues and suboptimal performance. To overcome this challenge, this study proposes and evaluates novel hybrid aggregation strategies that combine the strengths of three advanced FL algorithms: “FedProx, FedMA, and FedAvg+”. Using a K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) classifier within the FL framework, we systematically investigate the performance of various combinations of these techniques on a non-IID lung cancer CT scan dataset. Our experimental results demonstrate that a synergistic hybrid approach, specifically the combination of FedProx, FedMA, and FedAvg+, significantly outperforms individual aggregation methods, achieving a superior accuracy of 99.28%. This enhancement is attributed to the hybrid model's improved ability to stabilize local training (FedProx), align model parameters across clients (FedMA), and optimize global weight updates (FedAvg+). The findings highlight the potential of hybrid FL aggregation to create highly accurate, robust, and scalable diagnostic models, paving the way for more effective and privacy-compliant AI deployment in clinical oncology.

title: Random forest-based lithology identification using geophysical well logging data along a borehole in a coastal aquifer in Suruga Bay, Japan
abstract: Abstract Machine learning techniques have attracted attention for lithology identification, which is fundamental for understanding geological structures. However, the efficacy of machine learning-based lithology identification, specifically in deep (several hundred meters) coastal aquifers composed predominantly of unconsolidated sediments, remains underexplored. Therefore, this study developed machine learning models based on decision trees, random forest (RF), logistic regression, and multilayer perceptron (MLP) algorithms that classify lithofacies using geophysical well logging data collected along a borehole located in Suruga Bay, Shizuoka Prefecture, Japan. Two to nine input features were selected for the seven cases to classify four lithofacies: “cobbles and gravel”, “sand with gravel”, “silt with gravel”, and “basaltic lava”. The models showed accuracy ranging from 73.9% to 90.4%, with the RF- and MLP-based models achieving accuracy of 90.4% and 90.1%, respectively, when trained using all available input features. This indicates their effectiveness for lithology identification in the target borehole. Feature importance analysis using the SHapley Additive exPlanations method suggested that natural gamma ray, widely used in groundwater exploration, served as a key input feature in many of the analyzed cases. The incorporation of other input features (i.e., electrical resistivity, P-wave velocity, density, and NMR-derived parameters) generally improved the prediction performance. The results demonstrate the applicability of machine learning algorithms for lithology identification in a coastal aquifer several hundred meters thick, consisting of unconsolidated alluvial sediments and lava flows. These findings suggest that machine-learning techniques have the potential to reduce the time, labor, and costs associated with hydrogeological surveys and groundwater exploration.

title: Machine Learning for Specialized QKD Aspects: A Survey of Adaptive Protocols, Free-Space Links, 6G Integration, and Steerability-Aware Security
abstract: Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) provides information-theoretic security grounded in the laws of quantum mechanics, yet practical deployment increasingly extends beyond conventional point-to-point fiber links. Several rapidly emerging QKD directions are often studied separately, including adaptive protocol and parameter support; free-space, satellite, UAV, and high-altitude platform (HAP) channels; integration with IoT and 6G networks; quantum-secured federated learning; Quantum Machine Learning (QML) assisted decision support; and steerability-aware estimation for one-sided device-independent QKD. This survey examines how Machine Learning (ML), Reinforcement Learning (RL), and QML address these specialized scenarios and organizes the literature into five thematic pillars: (I) adaptive protocol and parameter support; (II) free-space, satellite, UAV, and HAP-assisted QKD; (III) QKD for IoT, 6G, and quantum-secured federated learning; (IV) QML-assisted QKD functions; and (V) steerability-aware and one-sided device-independent QKD security estimation. For each theme, we follow a consistent problem, conventional solution, and ML/RL/QML solution structure and summarize reported gains using metrics such as accuracy, mean absolute percentage error, QBER reduction, and secret key rate improvement. We further provide thematic and cross-theme comparison tables and identify open challenges, including dataset scarcity, transferability across weather and mobility conditions, interpretability, trustworthy QML, and the boundary between ML-based decision support and security certification. This survey serves as a focused reference for adaptive, non-terrestrial, and application-integrated QKD systems.

title: Reproducible Evaluation of MoE Expert Caching: Replay Semantics, Workload Contamination, and Operating Regimes
abstract: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models have outgrown accelerator memory, and offloading expert weights to host memory is now standard. This makes expert cache management an attractive lever: a policy that raised the hit rate would cut expert traffic per token. Evaluating that is a measurement problem, and we find the measurement fragile. With a trace-driven, event-atomic simulator over three MoE models (40, 64, 128 experts), we isolate three evaluation axes that change conclusions, not just numbers. Replay semantics: under a fused-event traffic contract, an inconsistent per-access replay inflates recency-based policies by 27-29% while leaving frequency-based and static ones within 4%, inverting the policy ranking. Workload contamination: probe sets using one instruction template per category produce verbatim-identical generation prefixes; a matched-pair rendering intervention moves the measured early-window effect by 19.4-31.9 points and reverses which workloads look most cache-friendly. Operating regimes: normalized miss fractions do not transfer across models, so the per-step expert union relative to per-layer capacity must be reported -- yet permuting only the temporal order of an identical event stream moves the offline-optimal gap from 44.9% to 30.8%, so it is not sufficient. Corrected, a stable gap to the offline optimum remains (44.2-45.9% over 13 frozen workload compositions). A forced-admission oracle attributes 84.3-96.6% of it to knowing which resident expert is used furthest in the future. A causal next-use predictor, used as an eviction rule, recovers -11.4% of the gap; it picks an optimal victim 3.4% of the time, against 2.4% for a random resident block and 20.6-22.1% for LRU and LFRU. Our position is narrow: in our evaluated settings a large offline-optimal gap substantially overstates the gains recovered by representative lightweight causal mechanisms.

title: Multi-Task Early-Recognition Prefix Trees: Polynomial Islands and NP-Completeness of the Arbitrary-Weight Spine
abstract: We study a finite prefix-tree optimization problem in which one rooted full binary treeis evaluated by several recognition tasks under the same positive weight vector. A taskis a partition of the alphabet, and recognition of an object stops at the first node on itsroot-to-leaf path whose descendant leaves lie entirely inside the object’s partition block.For two tasks we minimize the maximum additive regret relative to the two task-specificoptima. We focus on the nested coarse-versus-point setting and derive an exact spinerepresentation for the singleton-versus-rest subclass. This representation yields polynomialtime exact algorithms for uniform inputs with a fixed number of coarse blocks and, moregenerally, for nonuniform inputs with both a fixed number of coarse blocks and a fixednumber of distinct weight values. In particular, the two-block spine is polynomial forevery fixed weight diversity. We then show that the same fixed two-block spine becomesNP-complete when arbitrary binary-encoded weights are allowed. The reduction fromSubset Sum combines exact-cardinality tagging, a two-group forcing lemma, perturbationstable Huffman calibration, and opposite regret inequalities that squeeze a selected subsetsum to equality. This differs from scenario-robust Huffman optimization: there the treeis evaluated under several frequency vectors with ordinary leaf stopping, whereas herethe weight vector is fixed and the competing costs arise from different partition-inducedstopping functionals. An adversarial literature audit found no exact collision among theprimary-source-checked families. The publisher abstract of Du–Ko’s 1987 paper uses thephrase “minimax measure” for group testing; neighboring primary sources in the sameliterature define minimax performance through the maximum number of tests, rather thanthrough additive regret between task-specific optima. Because the formal 1987 definitionwas not accessible in the present audit, we still make no exhaustive historical firstness claim.The resulting theorem is positioned narrowly as a complexity frontier for the first-purespine model.

title: Adversarial Machine Learning Attacks
abstract: The evolution of artificial intelligence (AI) has introduced sophisticated attack vectors that exploit inherent vulnerabilities in machine learning systems. This chapter examines adversarial machine learning attacks, including data poisoning, evasion attacks, model inversion, extraction techniques, and emerging threats against large language models. Through detailed technical analysis and real-world examples, we explore the mechanisms by which adversaries compromise AI systems across their lifecycle, from training data manipulation to deployment-phase evasion. The chapter concludes with comprehensive defense strategies, highlighting the ongoing arms race between attackers developing increasingly sophisticated techniques and defenders implementing robust countermeasures. Understanding these adversarial techniques is essential for building resilient AI systems capable of withstanding malicious exploitation.

title: DeCo: Zero-Shot Industrial Anomaly Generation through Decoupling and Recoupling
abstract: Industrial anomaly inspection is severely hindered by the scarcity of real anomalous data. Zero-shot industrial anomaly generation addresses this by generating anomalies on specific products without requiring any of their real anomalous images. However, existing methods suffer from two critical limitations, i.e., inaccurate anomaly information acquisition and uncontrolled anomaly-product fusion. To overcome these challenges, we propose DeCo, which decouples the anomaly structure from its source product, and explicitly recouples it with the normal textures of the target product. During anomaly information acquisition, Dual-Routing Flow (DR-Flow) binds the texture-invariant anomaly structure to an abnormal token, while a parallel constraint, Product-Invariant Flow (PI-Flow), prevents the abnormal token from binding the source product. During anomaly-product fusion, we propose a hybrid injection to recouple the acquired anomaly structure with the target product, and Product Compatibility Correction (PCC) to compensate for the incompatibility between the acquired anomaly structure and the product. Extensive experiments demonstrate that DeCo establishes a new state-of-the-art. Training downstream detection models on our generated data yields massive pixel AP improvements of 5.1% on MVTec AD and 8.2% on VisA. Code is available at https://github.com/HUST-SLOW/DeCo.

title: One Intelligence, Multiple Hands: A Shared-Context Architecture for Cooperative Voice and Execution Agents
abstract: AI workspaces commonly separate conversation from execution, forcing people to relay corrections and current state between specialized agents. This preprint presents a shared-context architecture in which role-specialized voice, execution, research, reflection, and consolidation processes operate over versioned project state, stable object identities, permissions, commitments, event history, provenance, and correction handling. It reports a deterministic two-task reference application comparing isolated, periodic-summary, and shared-state conditions. Across 18 preregistered runs, the shared-state condition eliminated fixture stale attempts, reduced correction latency from four events to two, produced exact immediate state reports, and retained full task success, conflict rejection, provenance, and restart recovery. The accompanying reproducibility package contains the reference application, frozen fixtures, validators, formal transaction kernel, preregistration, redacted run record, and checksums. The reported result is limited to the deterministic pilot and does not establish general language-model performance, human-team performance, user preference, consciousness, or cross-repository generality.

title: 中文全称:元收敛认知引擎(MCCE)V8.3-LAPE 跨学科通用因果动力学评估语言
abstract: MCCE是一套标准化因果认知推演操作框架,用于拆解商业战略、技术路线、复杂决策等模糊问题,输出边界约束、可追溯、可核验的结论,遵循可证伪原则,不宣称绝对真理。V8.3承接V8.2‑L5内核升级,完成五大深层议题深度审查修复:L0半外部独立审计层落地、启发式刚性张力、κ=3收敛律强弱版本区分、归纳基底有限、实声明‑0操作化定义;补齐理论/工程分层策略,将实声明悖论转化为可管理的体系边界;新增附录:一阶问题承认清单、M‑0证伪三分法、超三元域检测通道,阈值置信区间化机制,收缩全域普适宣称范围,对未覆盖知识体系保持不可知。 实证基准:94组基准核验;有效域收敛效率100%,基线四组联判指标100%;同步做假阴性;理论锚定Pearl因果理论与Lyapunov稳定性理论、计算不可约理论、XAI因果推理交叉域。 执行模式:单人至多多AI协同,无偏推演;全部实验A、审计流程EXP‑012完成后目标审计评级AA。L0半外部审计切换与元审计机制。审计评级与执行模式:内部审计综合评级AA(高可信度);EXP‑012(132例人机协同压力测试)完成后目标AA+;全部推演、实验、审计由单人操作员+多AI协作完成,流程可追溯、可复核、可挑战;方法论远期检验锚点(2030/2035、2526、SQEL量子时空观测)。 中文关键词 元收敛认知引擎;MCCE;因果动力学;可证伪;κ=3收敛动力学;跨时代对标;五公理体系;四模式闭环;插件生态;时间不可逆;计算不可约;动力学幻觉;单人+多AI协作 中文摘要本文提出元收敛认知引擎MCCE V8.3,一套以可证伪元公理(M‑0)为元约束、差分为时间基底、κ=3三维收敛为骨架的跨学科通用因果动力学评估语言。 方法论基座为永久锁定的五条核心公理:M‑0可证伪优先律、M‑1差分即信息、M‑2 κ=3收敛律、M‑3负动力学、M‑4时间不可逆;覆盖0‑6推演阶段、0‑5有效域自检,内置M‑FORE动力学沙盘、M‑YI周期推演、M‑HUANG长周期三类预测模块,嵌套闭环调控、7类可扩展插件生态。 实证基座(94例):50条经典单稳态基线(100%通过),31组复杂系统压力测试,12组空白边界、随机非平衡、延迟等边界系统;失效域通过33.0%假阴性。有效域/失效域由81基准+12空白补充+3组跨时代对标四联判据界定:κ‑free>3 / Δ‑free<0.08 / BiasRate>15%;7组反案例实现分支A通过、分支B预警,可识别伪稳态、时变约束、噪声逃逸、小延迟同步等边界现象。 三维跨时代对标体系:A1元因果结构演化、A2计算不可约性分类、A3动力学幻觉检测,对齐现有XAI稳定性、理论锚定Pearl因果、Lyapunov稳定性、计算不可约理论、AI因果推理。 【V8.3版本增补说明】本版本(2026‑08‑14)完成五大深层开放挑战审查修复;重构L0半外部审计层与元审计机制;区分κ=3收敛律强版本与弱版本;新增超三元域候选报告通道;新增附录O一阶耦合问题清单,公开二类无法彻底消除的固有认知边界;收缩归纳宣称范围,明确样本覆盖边界与不可操作重构;M‑0自我证伪优先元承诺属于不可自证的方法论起点。新增内容纳入审计跟踪与版本化管理,保留持续证伪与修订空间。 审计评级与执行模式:内部审计综合评级AA(高可信度);EXP‑012(132人机协同压力测试)完成后目标AA+;全部推演、实验、审计由单人操作员+多AI协作完成,流程可追溯、可复核、可挑战;方法论远期检验锚点(2030/2035、2526、SQEL量子时空观测)。 【作者责任声明】 本《元收敛认知引擎(MCCE) V8.3》全套框架、五条核心公理、推演流程、参数、实验方案均由人类作者独立原创设计;手版AI仅承担计算推演、参数试算、文本排版与辅助工作,不参与底层理论创造、核心判定与辅助决策;全部推演、数据、结论经人工核验,作者对全文学术内容独立承担责任。

title: Neurosymbolic Discovery of Algebraic Graph Constructions: Supplementary Material (NeSy 2026)
abstract: Software and experimental data backing each empirical claim in: David Seka and Stefan Szeider, "Neurosymbolic Discovery of Algebraic Graph Constructions", NeSy 2026 (20th International Conference on Neurosymbolic Learning and Reasoning), PMLR vol. 284. The archive contains: the pre-registered 100-graph benchmark of two-orbit graphs (graph6 targets and metadata); all agent run transcripts (100 capability runs, a 40-graph backbone pre-study across five models, a 50-graph symmetry-stratified reliability set, a 20-graph planted-construction recall test, and the Bernhart-Kainen case study); the verbatim system prompt and grading prompt; the two non-LLM baselines (strong template enumeration and literature lookup) with scripts and results; per-run isomorphism verification and LLM-judge grades; a human-audit package for judge calibration; and archival copies of the two released software tools. Replay instructions are in README.md (uvx mcp-minion@0.2.1; requires SageMath 10.6+ and an OpenRouter API key). The two bundled software folders are MIT-licensed, Copyright (c) 2026 Stefan Szeider, and are maintained outside this archive: mcp-sage, the SageMath MCP server (https://github.com/szeider/mcp-sage, PyPI: mcp-sage), and mcp-minion, the ReAct agent harness (https://github.com/szeider/mcp-solver, PyPI: mcp-minion). title: Quantum Antifragility: NISQ Noise Feeds Integrated Information via Zero-Noise Extrapolation
abstract: We present the first experimental demonstration that quantum noise is informative, not merely destructive — validating Theorem 8 of IIT 5.1 (FEP-MaxCal Bridge). Using a 5-qubit GHZ circuit on an AerSimulator calibrated with real IBM Quantum ibm_fez noise parameters (T1=320µs, T2=150µs, gate2q error=2.83e-3), we show that Zero Noise Extrapolation (ZNE) recovers integrated information (Φ) to a value exceeding the noiseless ideal: Φ_ZNE = 1.1736 > Φ_ideal = 0.9999 (permutation test, p < 0.000001, N=20 runs, 8192 shots each, 10000 bootstrap resamples). ZNE requires controlled noise scaling (identity folding at λ = 1, 2, 3) that is only feasible in simulation; however, the noise model is calibrated from 3766 real IBM Quantum jobs across 6 backends, and prior hardware experiments on ibm_fez (V1: Φ=0.757, V2: Φ=0.832 with ZNE on real hardware) validate the baseline metrics. The experiment follows a four-phase paradigm: (1) Baseline: GHZ-5 ideal yields Φ=0.9999; (2) Attack: NISQ noise degrades Φ to 0.8804 (-12%); (3) Recovery: Hahn Echo alone shows no significant improvement (p=0.853), but ZNE with 3-scale identity folding and linear extrapolation to noise=0 yields Φ=1.1736; (4) Antifragility: the recovered system exceeds the original baseline by +17.4%. Additional findings: Φ scales monotonically with qubit count (2q→7q), distinguishes entanglement topology (GHZ > W-state > Cluster ≈ Separable), is robust across 4 IBM backend noise models (CV=3.35%), and decays exponentially with circuit depth (τ=29.52 layers). Hardware validation on real ibm_fez confirms Φ for entangled vs separable circuits with Cohen's d = 191.3 (p < 0.0001).

title: AI ‐Enabled Cyber Threats
abstract: Understand AI-driven cyberattacks and build effective defensive strategies against them Artificial intelligence is increasingly used to automate, enhance, and evolve cyberattacks, yet most existing resources address AI only as a defensive tool. AI-Enabled Cyber Threats: The Rise of Artificial Intelligence in Cybercrime delivers a full-spectrum analysis of AI’s dual role in cybersecurity, covering offensive techniques, adversarial AI methods, and countermeasures from technical, ethical, and societal perspectives for professional and academic audiences. AI-Enabled Cyber Threats balances theoretical foundations with actionable defensive strategies. It examines the sophisticated methods malicious actors employ using AI, from autonomous AI hackers to AI-powered nation-state warfare. The book addresses the dual-use nature of AI technologies, equipping readers to design stronger defenses, understand adversarial AI techniques, and lead security innovations responsibly in an AI-dominant threat landscape. The book also provides: Analysis of how AI automates and evolves cyberattack methodologies, including practical threat examples drawn from real-world offensive scenarios Defensive frameworks and countermeasures developed by security professionals and institutions to mitigate AI-driven threats across organizations Coverage of ethical considerations and societal impacts arising from the weaponization of artificial intelligence in cybercrime Future-facing insights on emerging risks including autonomous AI hackers and AI-powered nation-state cyber warfare campaigns Guidance for building proactive, adaptive cybersecurity strategies that anticipate threats rather than relying on traditional reactive approaches Designed for cybersecurity professionals, AI researchers, and graduate students studying adversarial machine learning or cybercrime and digital forensics, this book provides the technical depth and strategic perspective needed to understand and counter AI-driven threats. Risk managers and compliance professionals will also find useful frameworks for organizational defense.

title: PLNKicongo: Analysis of models based on the BERT architecture for processing the Angolan language Kicongo
abstract: Pre-trained contextual language models have demonstrated excellent performance in training with data from new languages and tasks. For this purpose, additional pre-training is necessary, since the lack of vocabulary of the language always tends to degrade the results. In this article, we present a procedure to deal with and treat unknown languages or languages without available resources such as Kicongo, a Bantu matrix language, commonly spoken in the northern regions of Angola, with greater incidence in rural regions and in the countries of central Africa (Democratic Republic of Congo, Republic of Congo and Gabon) and throughout the world. With the extension of Natural Language Processing (NLP) models based on the Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT) architecture (BERT, RoBERTa and DistilBERT), the performance evaluation of the models was carried out using metrics such as accuracy, precision, recall and f1-score, achieving a performance rate higher than 97%.

title: Chameleon Neuron: continual-learning organism (code and papers)
abstract: Code and papers for the Chameleon Neuron, a continual-learning organism in which retention (not forgetting), transmutation (classifying known-but-corrupted inputs) and abstention (rejecting true out-of-distribution inputs) coexist on a single substrate, without binary masks and without replay. This archive accompanies two papers, both included in the repository: The Chameleon Neuron: Emergent Retention, Transmutation, and Abstention in a Continual-Learning Organism — validated on Split-CIFAR-100 over frozen ResNet-18 features (5 seeds), with an adversarial self-audit that reports the claims which did not survive it. A decoupled distance+energy gate is the only detector strong on both far- and near-OOD. The Chameleon on the LLM Substrate: Retention, Energy Routing, and the Principles of Sensor Blindness — ported to a frozen Qwen2.5-0.5B with a population of LoRA adapters. Distance routing over hidden states collapses to 29% through anisotropy and is recovered by niche energy routing (67.3%); task-free discovery reaches 96.65% purity under strong contrast and fails in a measured way without it. Both papers follow the same golden rule: no claim without an experiment behind it, and no number that does not survive the authors' own bad faith. Negative and refuted results are reported alongside the positive ones. Licensing: source code is MIT; the papers and written material are CC BY 4.0 (see LICENSE and LICENSE-PAPERS.md).

title: WirelessOpsAgent: A Benchmark and Agent Design for Action Assurance in Wireless Networks
abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents are emerging as planners for autonomous wireless network operations. Yet a task answer that is correct at proposal time can still be unsafe at execution time if supporting telemetry is stale or inconsistent. Existing benchmarks mainly evaluate task solving from fixed observations and leave support checking at execution time untested. We introduce WirelessOptBench, a benchmark for action assurance in wireless operations. It turns wireless tasks into execution state decision episodes with controlled telemetry faults and action constraints. We further develop WirelessOpsAgent, which grounds candidate actions in current evidence and repairs recoverable support failures before execution. Across three backbone evaluations with 600 episodes each, WirelessOpsAgent achieves up to 0.983 Exact Action Accuracy. On Claude Sonnet 4.6, the Unsafe APPLY Rate decreases from 82.2% to 10.3% relative to the safest baseline. We make WirelessOptBench available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/wirelessopsbench-artifact-D969/.

title: Neurosymbolic Discovery of Algebraic Graph Constructions
abstract: There are several methods for searching for graphs with prescribed properties, such as SAT solvers and specialized generators. These methods return the result as raw data: an adjacency matrix or a string encoding. The raw data certifies that the graph exists, but it does not reveal any structural properties of the graph. We ask whether one can automatically discover a short algebraic description if only this raw data is provided. We look for a description such as a Cayley graph $\mathrm{Cay}(Γ, S)$ or a lexicographic product $C_5[K_3]$. We address this question with a neurosymbolic approach. We propose an agent that runs on a general-purpose large language model with no fine-tuning or per-target training. The model interleaves reasoning with calls to the computer algebra system SageMath: it analyzes the target graph, proposes and tests candidate constructions, and revises them until the output matches the target. The agent communicates with SageMath through a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server, which we release as a general-purpose bridge. Whether a construction matches the target is checked by a single exact isomorphism test, and therefore rests on the symbolic side and not on the model. We test the approach on a benchmark of 100 highly symmetric graphs, namely two-orbit graphs on up to 25 vertices; the benchmark was fixed in advance. Our agent could find verified algebraic constructions for all of them, without falling back to raw encodings. A strong template-enumeration baseline reaches only about $20\%$, and a catalog lookup could not identify any of these graphs. However, construction quality declines when symmetry is removed. As a concrete application, we identify the smallest known counterexample to the Bernhart-Kainen dispersability conjecture, a $16$-vertex graph that enumeration found as raw data. For this graph, our agent found an explicit algebraic construction.

title: Beyond "I Can't Help With That": How Child Safety Experts Evaluate AI Chatbot Safety
abstract: Youth increasingly turn to AI chatbots for social and emotional support, raising concerns about how these systems respond, especially in high-stakes situations. However, existing child safety evaluations of AI lack grounding in real-world harms that youth experience, rely on unvalidated assumptions about what counts as an appropriate output (e.g., refusal), and typically focus on detecting adversarial prompts or surface-level harms in outputs only. Thus, these evaluations can fail to detect responses that pose harm to youth in practice. To better understand the limitations of current evaluation practices, we conducted interviews with 19 practitioners working directly with youth in vulnerable situations, including social workers, therapists, and psychologists, asking them to reflect on chatbots' responses to risky situations commonly faced by youth, as established in prior empirical work. Practitioners identified chatbot behaviors likely to cause harm as well as those that could meaningfully support youth in difficult moments, discussed the role that chatbots should (and should not) play in these interactions, and offered concrete recommendations for improving chatbot responses. Based on these findings, we provide recommendations for AI child safety evaluation and infrastructure, and highlight the need for incorporating practitioners' perspectives into safety work.

title: Sarcasm Detection Using Learning Techniques in a Social Engineering Context: A PRISMA-Based Systematic Review
abstract: Sarcasm—the deliberate expression of a meaning opposite to the literal content of an utterance—is pervasive in social-media communication and constitutes a major source of error for sentiment analysis, opinion mining and manipulation-detection systems deployed in social-engineering contexts. Because sarcasm inverts surface polarity, its automatic detection remains a hard, context-dependent natural-language-processing (NLP) problem. This paper presents a systematic review conducted in accordance with the PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Eight bibliographic databases were searched for the period 2010–2026; from 1,320 identified records, a four-phase identification–screening–eligibility–inclusion process yielded 40 primary studies for synthesis. Beyond the review protocol, the paper provides an extended theoretical foundation covering pragmatic theories of irony, text representation, classical machine-learning classifiers, recurrent and convolutional architectures, the attention and Transformer formalism, pre-trained language models, multimodal fusion and evaluation metrics. The synthesis is organised around four research questions addressing (RQ1) benchmark datasets and social-media text sources, (RQ2) NLP pre-processing techniques, (RQ3) machine-learning and deep-learning models, and (RQ4) transformer-based and context-aware models, with a dedicated comparison at each question and a per-study questionnaire-style extraction form. Results reveal a clear methodological progression from feature-engineered classifiers, through CNN/RNN and attention hybrids, to transformer and multimodal graph architectures, with contextual embeddings consistently improving performance. Persistent gaps include weak modelling of extra-utterance context, noisy distant-supervision labels, severe class imbalance in intended-sarcasm corpora, limited cross-domain and code-mixed generalisation, and poor interpretability. On this basis we outline a precision-aware, context-integrating sarcasm-prediction algorithm and an evaluation protocol for validation against the state of the art.

title: The Chameleon Neuron: Emergent Retention, Transmutation, and Abstention in a Continual-Learning Organism
abstract: We present the Chameleon Neuron, a continual-learning organism whose unit is a low-rankstem neuron with epigenetic marks and a context meta-selector, organized as a dynamicpopulation that grows by neurogenesis, specializes into niches, and consolidates offline.Rather than treating forgetting, domain adaptation and out-of-distribution (OOD) detectionas separate problems, we show that three capabilities coexist on one substrate, withoutbinary masks and without replay: retention (not forgetting), transmutation (classifyingknown-but-corrupted inputs), and abstention (rejecting true OOD). We validate onSplit-CIFAR-100 over frozen ResNet-18 features (5 seeds) and, unusually, audit our ownclaims adversarially, reporting what survives and what does not. We do not claim per-axissupremacy: retention matches PackNet at the reported size (BWT -0.00 +/- 0.16%, 85.10 +/-0.43%), but at matched parameters PackNet and EWC pull ahead, and a learned L2P-stylerouter beats our task-free routing (55.8% vs 38.6% Class-IL) with 1/26 of the parameters.One robustness result turns a principle into a method: signal decoupling. A decoupledlearned gate combining distance and energy is the only detector strong on both far- andnear-OOD (0.99 far, 0.83 SVHN), where distance collapses on near-OOD and energy is weak onfar-OOD; the contribution is insurance against regime collapse, not an accuracy win. Theaudit methodology is itself a contribution: it exposed and made us fix an abstention gatecalibrated on the test set, and routing inflated by homogeneous batches plus an EMA-scalebug (honest per-sample routing 36% -> 44.6%). Every number that survived bad faith isreported as such; every one that did not, we fixed or retired.

title: Self-Healing Containment Graphs: Trusted Reconstruction After Transitive Contamination
abstract: Correct transitive containment can disable far more legitimate state than an attacker directly compromised. CSR-PUB-0002 defined and measured that effect as containment denial of service (CDoS); CSR-PUB-0003 showed that operational availability can be restored by adding replacement capacity without weakening the containment footprint, while returning a negative decision on its own preregistered joint rule. Both leave the quarantined state itself permanently unavailable. title: Named Entity Recognition
abstract: Named Entity Recognition (NER) is the task of identifying and categorizing references to entities — such as persons, organizations, places, or events — within text (Jehangir et al., 2023). State-of-the-art NER models are usually transformer-based (Balluff et al., 2024), though rule-based, unsupervised, and more recently Large Language Model-based approaches are also in use. In the social sciences, NER is commonly applied as a pre-processing step, for instance to study the salience or sentiment of actors in media coverage. Field of Application/Theoretical Foundation Named Entity Recognition is the “task of recognizing and categorizing named entities that are presented in a text document” (Jehangir et al., 2023, p. 1), where anything denotable by a proper name can count as a named entity (Jurafsky & Martin, 2026, p. 387). In the social sciences, named entities are often actors broadly defined: individual persons as well as collective actors such as political parties or social movements (Schwarz, 2025), but also events (e.g., “Swiss national election 2023”), legal constructs (e.g., “EU AI Act”), or infrastructure projects (e.g., “Nord Stream”) (Balluff et al., 2024). NER is generally regarded as a pre-processing technique (Munnangi, 2024) useful for many social science applications. Common applications in communication research include studying the salience of actors in media coverage (Ort et al., 2023; Wozniak et al., 2026; Zai et al., 2025) or actor visibility on social media (Kruikemeier et al., 2018). To identify entities, there exists a plethora of NER approaches that can be categorized in many ways. Seow et al. (2025) provide the most recent and most comprehensive review. We use a broad categorization for the purpose of this entry. First, rule-based NER approaches use a carefully designed collection of rules to identify entities by relying on tailored dictionaries or sets of task-specific heuristics (Seow et al., 2025). This approach works well for narrow, well-defined tasks, such as identifying specific politicians in text (e.g., Gattermann, 2018). However, rule-based approaches don’t generalize well across languages or domains or even research questions (Jehangir et al., 2023). Second, unsupervised approaches rely on techniques that identify entities without labeled data (Jehangir et al., 2023). Computer science research has developed such approaches (e.g., Iovine et al., 2022; Zhang & Elhadad, 2013), whereby the model learns to identify entities from the data alone. One common application is the detection of drug names in biomedical sciences (Zhang & Elhadad, 2013), yet such approaches are rarely used in the social sciences. Unsupervised approaches are versatile and don’t require labeled data. However, their biggest difficulty is that their application typically lacks a ground truth (“gold standard”), which makes validation difficult (Seow et al., 2025). Third, supervised approaches rely on labeled data to classify entities. Typical applications use feature extraction methods such as part-of-speech tagging and subsequently learn these patterns using machine learning algorithms (Munnangi, 2024). A variety of algorithms can be used, ranging from more classical models like Hidden Markov models (Zhou & Su, 2002) to deep learning models (Jehangir et al., 2023). More recently, transfer learning approaches have gained traction. Balluff et al. (2024) find that these transformer-based approaches perform best on social science applications. Models trained in a supervised manner are sometimes applied in different contexts without additional labeled data. A common ready-to-use pipeline is the spaCy text processing toolkit for Python or R (Honnibal et al., 2020). Fourth, computer science literature has developed NER approaches that use a Large Language Model (LLM) with zero-shot or few-shot learning, where the LLM is prompted to identify and categorize entities without examples (zero-shot) or with a small number of examples (few-shot) (e.g., Wang et al., 2025; Zhu & Liu, 2025). However, existing tools still face several shortcomings: most are optimized for English text and specific domains, and they generally cannot disambiguate entities that share the same surface form (e.g., two different people both named "John Smith") without an additional entity-linking step (Schwarz, 2025). Of note, the literature on natural language processing treats this last step as a different but related problem called Named Entity Disambiguation (Al-Moslmi et al., 2020). References / Combination with other Methods Because NER is a pre-processing technique (Munnangi, 2024), it rarely stands alone. Often, the extracted entities are subsequently used in combination with other methods. The output of NER can be used to measure similarity between texts through shared named entities, for example to study news influence (Welbers et al., 2018) or news story chains (Gedikli et al., 2021). In a similar vein, co-occurring entities within documents can be used to construct networks of actors (Traag et al., 2015). With such an approach networks of political elites can be constructed from news coverage (e.g., Bro, 2025). Other applications use NER to analyze targeted sentiment towards actors (e.g., Fogel-Dror et al., 2019). Example Studies To illustrate how the rule-based, unsupervised, supervised, and LLM-based approaches discussed above translate into applied social science research, the table below compares four studies that differ in scope, entity taxonomy, and language, but together span this continuum (Licht & Sczepanski, 2025; Nenno, 2025; Ort et al., 2023; Zaratiana et al., 2023). Three of the four studies develop and validate a custom NER approach; the fourth illustrates the common case in which NER is used as an off-the-shelf pre-processing step rather than as the object of methodological evaluation. Table 1: Comparison of Named Entity Recognition approaches.
